zh: (1923-91) a British businessman, publisher and newspaper owner, born in Czechoslovakia. He came to Britain in 1940 and received the Military Cross for his military achievements in the Second World War. He first became rich through his publishing company, the Pergamon Press. However, in 1969, an official investigation into the company decided that he was not a suitable person to run a company. He was also at this time a Labour Member of Parliament, a position he held from 1964 to 1970. Maxwell built up a large business empire and became one of the most powerful people in the newspaper industry. In 1984 he bought Mirror Group Newspapers and so became the owner of the Daily Mirror, the Sunday Mirror and The Sunday People, all popular British newspapers. Maxwell died when he fell from a boat and drowned. After his death it was discovered that he had illegally taken money from the pension funds of employees. His sons Kevin and Ian were prosecuted for financial crimes involving his companies but were found not guilty. Maxwell's reputation, however, was destroyed.

zh: (1771-1858) a Welsh industrialist whose ideas on social reform (= changes to improve society) influenced the development of the Co-operative Movement and trade unions in Britain. zh: (1788-1850) one of the most important British politicians of the early 19th century and one of the people who started the modern Conservative Party. zh: (1274-1329) the king of Scotland from 1306 until his death. zh: （尤指阻断铁路或公路交通的）公众集会示威（或游行）
en: a public meeting or march (= organized walk by many people) at which people show that they are protesting against or supporting somebody/something, especially one that involves blocking a railway or road
ex: Activists staged a rail roko to protest against the minister’s decision.
活动人士组织了阻断铁路集会，抗议部长的决定。

en: an actor’s part in a play, film, etc.
ex: She has landed the lead role (= the most important one) in a new play.
她在一部新戏中扮演了主角。

en: a person that people admire and try to copy
ex: We need positive role models for young women to aspire to.
我们需要年轻女子可以效仿的楷模。

en: to behave in the way somebody else would behave in a particular situation as part of a learning activity
ex: The children sang songs in French and role-played with puppets.
孩子们用法语唱歌，并与木偶一起扮演角色。

zh: 角色扮演游戏（参加者假扮成幻想作品等中的虚构人物进行冒险）
en: a game, often an online or computer game, in which players pretend to be imaginary characters who take part in adventures, especially in situations from fantasy literature

zh: a type of expensive watch of high quality, first made in 1908 in Switzerland. Rolex watches are often regarded as a sign of success or wealth
en: a type of expensive watch of high quality, first made in 1908 in Switzerland. Rolex watches are often regarded as a sign of success or wealth
ex: They beat him up and stole his Rolex.
他们殴打他并偷走了他的劳力士。

en: to turn over and over and move in a particular direction; to make a round object do this
ex: The ball rolled down the hill.
球滚下了山。

en: to be laughing so much that you can hardly control yourself
to to reduce the power or importance of something; to reverse the progress made with something
ex: Many of the gains made in the last 20 years have been rolled back.
过去20年中取得的许多成就已被取消。

zh: （敞篷汽车顶部起加固和保护作用的）翻车防护杆，防滚保护杆
en: a metal bar over the top of a car without a roof, used to make the car stronger and to protect passengers if the car turns over
the reading of a list of names to a group of people to check who is there
ex: Roll call will be at 7 a.m.
早上 7 点钟点名。

en: to open or close something by turning a handle
ex: He rolled down his car window and started shouting at them.
他摇下车窗，朝他们大声喊起来。

en: to arrive in great numbers or amounts
ex: Offers of help are still rolling in.
仍然不断有人表示愿意提供援助。
